name: When can drywall be patched versus fully replaced?

mainEntity.name: When can drywall be patched versus fully replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall repair involves fixing localized damage like small holes, cracks, dents, or plumbing cuts, whereas full replacement requires tearing down sheets down to the framing and hanging new panels. If water damage, mold, or extensive physical impact compromises the structural core of multiple panels, replacement makes more sense. For minor wall settling cracks, doorknob punctures, or small access holes cut during pipe repairs, patching is the faster and more affordable choice. A professional evaluates whether the surrounding drywall is stable and dry enough to hold joint compound securely.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall can be patched if the damage is localized and the sheet is structurally sound. Full replacement is necessary if wide areas suffer heavy water damage, mold, or structural failure.
